title: a remote box's database syncs the home box's learning
intention: A remote box keeps its own database and syncs it with the home box's (outline 11.3.5.1): every learning table the home box holds is on the remote box with the same owner and the same node rows, so live-tree reads and proofs mean the same on every box.
why: Measured 2026-11-12: akienasus's local db holds one *_nodes table and none of codemother's trees, while akiendelllinux's codemother_orient_nodes holds 688 rows. So 2b3d842bc118's clause_4_the_live_tables_are_hers reds on akienasus ('codemother_orient_nodes owner=None rows=0/531'), and outline 11.3.5.1 has no ticket.
traces_to: Outline 11.3.5.1 (a remote box syncs its db with the home box's; the local copy is fast and the sync is the backup) and 4.3.1.5.1.1 (a row number is the same on every box).
how: HELD FOR A DESIGN PASS before BUILDME (orchestrator, 2026-11-12: cast, don't build). Open: the sync's unit (the built per-nexus <owner>_<nexus>_nodes tables versus the outline's one long node list, 4.3.1.5.1), its transport (postgres replication versus a row copy over the bus through db_domain), and its direction (home to remote only, or both ways with home-reserved slots). The proof measures the outcome, which is fixed: tables, owners and node rows match the home box after a sync.

clauses.claim: after a sync on a remote box, every learning table the home box holds exists on the remote box with the same owner and at least the home box's node ids
a node row read on both boxes is identical

decisions.text: D1: the sync lives in db_domain, the database proxy device (outline 11.3); its mechanism is the design pass's to settle.
D2: the proof, one tooth per clause 1-2, beside db_domain; clause 3 is 2b3d842bc118's tooth run on akienasus.

out: cairn/devices/librarian (the slot reservation of 4.3.1.5.1.1 is the design pass's to place)

measured.saw: akienasus: psql -d cairn shows 1 *_nodes table; clause_4 bad list 'orient: codemother_orient_nodes owner=None rows=0/531 chart_orient_nodes owner=None', the same for all nine nexi
measured.how: psql -d cairn -Atc "select count(*) from pg_tables where tablename like '%_nodes'"; bin/cairn test cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother_learning_lands_in_its_own_tables.py
